skill.name: triaging-issues
skill.description: GitHub issue triage assistant for classification, duplicate detection, relationship mapping, quality checks, and triage workflow support.
skill.summary: Classify, prioritize, deduplicate, and organize GitHub issues with guided triage workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static alerts were reviewed in context and were mostly false positives from Markdown code fences, GitHub CLI helper scripts, /dev/null redirection, and safe subprocess argument lists. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, shell eval, or path traversal evidence was found. A medium semantic risk remains because authenticated helper scripts can modify GitHub issue and project state in bulk.

remediation.issue: Bulk issue actions can change live repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run and confirmation modes before closing issues, adding labels, comments, or project items.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts depend on broad user-provided filters.
remediation.suggestion: Print the matched issue list and require explicit approval before applying batch changes.

remediation.issue: Numeric command inputs are not consistently validated.
remediation.suggestion: Validate issue numbers, project numbers, and day counts before passing them to gh or date.

remediation.issue: External tool requirements are implicit in several workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Document required gh and jq versions, authentication scopes, and expected repository permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated GitHub Issue State Mutation
semantic_findings.description: The helper script can close issues, add comments, apply labels, and add project items using the active gh token. This is intended triage automation, but broad filters can alter many repository issues without a built-in preview step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly invoke gh issue close, gh issue comment, gh issue edit, and gh project item-add. The risk is operational state change rather than command execution, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Busy repositories accumulate duplicates, vague reports, and unclear priorities. This skill helps classify, validate, connect, and organize issues with repeatable triage steps.
actual_capabilities: Classifies issues by type, priority, scope, and effort using documented triage rules.
Searches for possible duplicates with GitHub CLI queries and helper scripts.
Maps related, blocking, and dependent issues from issue bodies and labels.
Checks issue quality for title, body, labels, reproduction steps, and environment details.
Provides response templates for missing information, duplicates, stale issues, and security reports.
Supports batch labels, stale issue searches, duplicate closure, and project board updates.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, jq, repository access, and an authenticated GitHub session.
Duplicate detection uses simple keyword and title matching, not deep semantic analysis.
Helper scripts can change live issues when executed, so review actions before running them.
Priority recommendations still need product, customer, and release context from maintainers.

use_cases.title: Daily Issue Triage
use_cases.description: Review new issues, assign labels, spot missing information, and prepare clear next actions.

use_cases.title: Dependency Planning
use_cases.description: Map blocked issues, related work, and recommended order for a sprint or milestone.

use_cases.title: Duplicate Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find likely duplicate reports, compare context, and draft respectful closure comments.

prompt_templates.title: Triage One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage GitHub issue #42. Classify its type, priority, scope, quality, and recommended labels.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicates
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether issue #42 is a duplicate. Compare likely matches and explain the confidence for each match.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Issue Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review issue #42 for missing details. Draft a concise maintainer comment that requests the needed information.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Batch Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all open unlabeled issues. Group them by type, priority, blockers, duplicates, and recommended maintainer actions.

output: Classification: bug, high priority, backend scope.
Quality: clear title and steps, but missing environment details.
Recommended actions: add bug and priority labels, request logs, and link related authentication issues.
Potential duplicate: issue #91 has the same error code and affected workflow.
Related but not duplicate: issue #77 mentions login but describes a timeout.
Recommendation: ask maintainers to confirm #91 before closing #108.

output_examples.input: Show which issues block the next release.
output: Ready to start: issues with no blockers and clear acceptance criteria.
Blocked: issues waiting on authentication and database migration work.
Suggested order: finish the shared blocker first, then schedule dependent profile and reset tasks.

best_practices: Review proposed labels, comments, and closures before applying changes to GitHub.
Use issue templates so triage decisions have consistent evidence.
Link duplicates and related issues clearly so reporters can follow the active thread.
anti_patterns: Bulk-closing issues based only on keyword matches.
Assigning priority labels without impact, urgency, and maintainer context.
Running helper scripts with broad filters before previewing the affected issue list.

faq.question: Does this skill require the GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts use gh and jq, and they need an authenticated GitHub session.

faq.question: Can it modify GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Some helper scripts can add labels, close duplicates, comment, and add project items.

faq.question: How does it find duplicates?
faq.answer: It searches existing issues by title, body keywords, labels, and simple similarity signals.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace maintainer judgment?
faq.answer: No. It prepares recommendations, but maintainers should confirm labels, closures, and priorities.

faq.question: Can it handle security reports?
faq.answer: It includes a security response template, but public issue details should follow the project security policy.
